beats: You've probably heard this one: before he started NVIDIA, Jensen Huang supposedly worked at a car wash. It's a nice story... but that's not how it happened.
What really happened behind that leather jacket was a lot HARDER.
And to see it, we have to rewind... way back, to nineteen seventy-two.
Jensen was nine years old. His uncle sent him to a boarding school in Kentucky, thinking it was a prestigious one... it turned out to be a tough boarding school.
His daily chore there? Cleaning the toilets, for about a HUNDRED boys. And his roommate was a seventeen-year-old.
At fifteen, he got his first job, at Denny's in Portland. Not washing cars, washing dishes... then busboy, then waiter.
But he didn't stay in the kitchen. He studied electrical engineering, then spent nine years designing chips at AMD and LSI Logic.
Until finally, in nineteen ninety-three, in a booth at a Denny's in San Jose, he and two colleagues sat down and planned a company... NVIDIA.
From cleaning boarding-school toilets and washing dishes, to building the most valuable chip company in the world.
So maybe the lesson is this: no job is too small, if you're building the habits that will take you to the top.
So what was your first job? Tell me in the comments.
